# Harrison

## Overview

- **Age:** Middle-aged  <sub>[v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v4 c3 P1](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0001)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007), [v2 c17 P8](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0008)</sub>

## Appearance

He is a short, fat, and bald man with a round face and prominent blue eyes. When anger overwhelms him, his face can turn purple with rage. Later on, after reuniting with his wife, he presents a remarkably neat and snug appearance.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c28 P8](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0008)_

## Personality

Initially presenting himself as a crabbed, lonesome, and crusty old bachelor, he prides himself on his blunt outspokenness. Though quick to express wrath, he displays an underlying kindness and sociable nature toward those he warms up to. He is notably hard to please regarding literature and prefers realism over high-flown phrasing.

_Sources: [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049), [v2 c4 P28](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0028), [v2 c20 P8](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0008), [v3 c12 P39](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0039), [v3 c12 P45](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0045)_

- Outspoken  <sub>[v2 c4 P28](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0028)</sub>

- Farming skills like harrowing and mowing hay  <sub>[v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007), [v2 c17 P8](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0008)</sub>

## Goals

- Puts on a white collar during business deals to avoid being cheated  <sub>[v2 c17 P78](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0078)</sub>

## History

Prior to settling in Avonlea, Mr. Harrison lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick. After his sister passed away, he fulfilled a promise to her by marrying Emily Scott, but the couple soon separated due to constant disagreements over his housekeeping habits and his profanity-uttering parrot, Ginger. Moving to Prince Edward Island to live as a solitary bachelor, he bought Robert Bell's farm adjoining the Cuthbert place. He gained an immediate reputation in Avonlea as a crank who had no set meal times and harbored a strong dislike for Mrs. Rachel Lynde. Over time, he struck up a warm friendship with Anne Shirley and befriended young Davy Keith. His estranged wife Emily unexpectedly rejoined him at his Avonlea home, leading to a happy reconciliation, an improvement in his personal appearance, and regular church attendance.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000), [v2 c20 P8](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0008), [v2 c25 P47](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0047), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059), [v2 c28 P8](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0008)_

## Quotes

> I’m a crusty, lonesome, crabbed old chap, but there’s something about that little girl makes me feel young again . . . and it’s such a pleasant sensation I’d like to have it repeated once in a while.  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

> That old nuisance of a Rachel Lynde was here again today, pestering me for a subscription towards buying a carpet for the vestry room. I detest that woman more than anybody I know. She can put a whole sermon, text, comment, and application, into six words, and throw it at you like a brick.  <sub>[v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000)</sub>

> Well, Anne, my easy times are over . . . all over. It’s neatness and tidiness for me for the rest of my natural life, I suppose.  <sub>[v2 c25 P47](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0047)</sub>

> It’ll be time for you to be getting a husband when you’re through Redmond. I don’t believe in putting marrying off too long—like I did.  <sub>[v3 c12 P76](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0076)</sub>
